name: Bysen
body:
BYSEN
CR 3

Pale gray in complexion with a deeply lined visage and glinting eyes, this short peculiar figure hefts a weathered axe.

XP 800
CN Small fey
Init +1; Senses low-light vision; Perception +12

DEFENSE

AC 15, touch 12, flat-footed 14 (+2 armor, +1 Dex, +1 natural, +1 size)
hp 33 (6d6+12)
Fort +4, Ref +6, Will +6
DR 5/cold iron

OFFENSE

Speed 30 ft.
Melee mwk battleaxe +8 (1d6+4/×3)
Spell-Like Abilities (CL 6th; concentration +8):

Constant—pass without trace
At will—daze (DC 12), know direction
5/day—lesser confusion (DC 13)
3/day—blur, hallucinatory terrain (DC 16), lost passage (DC 16), tree shape (Medium-sized stump only)

STATISTICS

Str 17, Dex 13, Con 14, Int 11, Wis 12, Cha 14
Base Atk +3; CMB +5; CMD 16
Feats Endurance, Power Attack, Skill Focus (Survival)
Skills Climb +12, Knowledge (geography) +9, Knowledge (nature) +9, Perception +12, Stealth +14 (+18 in forests), Survival +10; Racial Modifiers +2 Perception, +4 Stealth in forests
Languages Common, Sylvan
SQ twisted recovery
Gear leather armor, mwk battleaxe

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Twisted Recovery (Su)

A bysen’s magic can turn travelers around and cause them to lose their way, unable to retrace their steps.

However, in a world mystically turned sideways, twistedness can return a traveler to themselves. As a full-round action, a creature who has failed a saving throw against a bysen’s hallucinatory terrain or lost passage spell-like abilities can twist its hat, cloak, or anything else it is wearing. Doing this grants the creature a second saving throw against the effect at the same DC; this only allows one extra chance to successfully save against the effect.

Bysens (or, alternately, bysar) are mischievous gnome?like spirits who wander dense forests. Bysens use their uncanny magical talents to confuse travelers and lead them astray, twisting their senses and causing them to become hopelessly lost. With ashen skin and garbed in dull gray clothing, a bysen naturally blends with misty forest environs and may even be mistaken for an inconspicuous lichen-crusted tree stump.

ECOLOGY

Environment cold and temperate forests
Organization solitary
Treasure standard

The bysen is a mischief-maker and trickster but also acts as a warden of the forest and nature. Bysens meddle with foresters by upending loads of lumber and sabotaging or stealing transport carts. Bysens are also known to draw folk into the forest or entice intruders from their path, misleading them until they are completely lost. The bysen then plays pranks, such as stealing their belongings or leading them in circles. However, those who treat the forest with the proper respect may be spared a bysen’s interference.

Legends claim the bysen originated as a restless soul condemned to eternally wander the land for the crime of moving ancient boundary markers. It is also said that if someone finds and sets the misplaced markers aright, this will lift the curse. Other stories speak of the bysen’s penance, an eternal duty to slowly chop down the forest, but felling only a single tree each century.
